result:
**The plan:** Plan 84 closes finding 21: independence in execution. Before it, the SDD reviewer trusted the implementer's report as the only test evidence and was told not to re-run tests. The goal was a test result from a run the implementer did not report. The spec's other half, independence in authorship (finding 24), had already closed in plan 83, so this branch covers only execution.

**The build:** First, a micro-test kit and control arms ran at BASE to set baselines: controller 0/5, reviewer 4/5. Next came the core piece, a new `test-run` script. It records HEAD and tree state, runs the command once, writes a numbered run file that is never overwritten, with header lines and full output, and exits with the command's status. `task-done` in executing-plans was then rewired to call `test-run` and read its ledger command back from the run file. On top of the script, new controller text in `references/test-run.md` and related SDD files makes a failing run a fix round and has a killed run retried. A passing run's path goes to the reviewer. Last, the reviewer and re-review prompts compare the run file against the report and grade discrepancies as Important. Treatment arms scored 5/5. NOTICE, spec retirement and history records closed out the work.

**The project:** In SDD, DONE now leads to a controller test run before any review. Failing runs never reach a reviewer, and hidden skips or count mismatches become findings. SDD and executing-plans now share one run mechanism and run-file format. One item was deferred: a killed run leaves no partial output.
